title: Azure AZ-104 vs AWS SAA-C03: Which in 2026?
subtitle: The cloud associate showdown: Microsoft vs Amazon, sector by sector

pros: The largest cloud market in France and globally (~32% of the public cloud market in 2025).
Senior median salary of €65k in France (Hays/APEC 2026).
The most mature training ecosystem: ACG, Stéphane Maarek, Tutorials Dojo.
Recognized at virtually every tech-native company and cloud consultancy.
cons: A demanding technical exam — 65 questions, many complex scenarios.
Takes ~120 hours of prep with hands-on practice; without AWS Free Tier labs, failure is likely.
More 'architect' focused (trade-offs) than admin focused (day-to-day operations).
certs.bestFor: You're targeting Cloud Engineer / Solutions Architect roles at a tech-native company or cloud consultancy. The broadest job market.

pros: A very strong Azure market in banking, insurance and the public sector (Microsoft's legacy footprint).
Senior median salary of €60k in France, €78k in Luxembourg (Hays 2026).
More focused on day-to-day operations (deploy, configure, monitor) — practical for sysadmins changing careers.
Microsoft Learn (official) is free and excellent — no paid bootcamp needed.
cons: Valued less than the AWS cert at tech-native startups and scale-ups.
The Microsoft core (Active Directory, Entra ID) transfers less well outside Azure.
$165 exam, plus the Microsoft ecosystem (PowerShell + Azure CLI) to learn if you're not familiar with it.
certs.bestFor: You're targeting a traditional enterprise (banking, insurance, manufacturing, public sector) or you come from a Windows/sysadmin background.

verdicts.profile: You're new to cloud with no particular context and want the safest bet.
verdicts.why: AWS remains the broadest job market in 2026, and its training/community ecosystem is more mature. You'll find more openings.

verdicts.profile: You come from the Windows / sysadmin / Active Directory world.
verdicts.why: Your Microsoft background gives you a 30-40% head start on Entra ID, Windows networking and PowerShell. A much gentler learning curve.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a bank, an insurer, or the public sector.
verdicts.why: These sectors have long-standing Microsoft enterprise agreements and run heavily on Azure. An AWS cert is seen as a bonus, but Azure is expected.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting FAANG or a tech-native scale-up (Datadog, Doctolib, Mistral, etc.).
verdicts.why: The dominant tech-native stack = AWS. Some use Azure, but most cloud opportunities there are AWS-first.

verdicts.profile: You want to set yourself up for freelance / cloud consulting.
verdicts.why: Average freelance AWS day rates are higher in France (Free-Work 2026: €600-800 vs €550-700 for equivalent Azure work), and more engagements are available.

tldr: AWS SAA if you're targeting tech-native companies, startups or freelance work. AZ-104 if you're targeting banking, insurance, the public sector, or you come from the Microsoft world. Both are solid — choose by target sector, not by the 'best' technology.
